stories.headline: Coast Guard finds debris from the missing Boston-bound medical jet off Nantucket
stories.summary: Coast Guard crews off Nantucket have found debris confirmed to be from the missing Boston-bound medical jet, and the search for the six people aboard is still underway. The Canadian-registered Gulfstream G-100, operated by Latitude Air Ambulance, left Bermuda at 12:41 a.m. Saturday with four crew and two passengers headed to Logan for medical care. The FAA lost contact and issued a search alert at 1:20 a.m. Bermuda’s premier said the island is praying they are found safe. The search sits about 13 nautical miles offshore and covers roughly 30 by 20 nautical miles.

stories.headline: Trump rallies in Ohio for Jon Husted as the Senate race with Sherrod Brown tightens
stories.summary: President Trump took his midterm swing into Vandalia, outside Dayton, on Saturday to boost appointed GOP Sen. Jon Husted against former Sen. Sherrod Brown in a race Republicans now call dead even. Trump told reporters Brown is “horrible” and that voters already threw him out once. Sen. Tim Scott said the gap has closed to a tie, while Republicans worry data-center politics and a Springfield truck-plant layoff of nearly 1,400 people days before the rally are weighing on Husted in a state Democrats need to flip the Senate.

stories.headline: Prosecutor: two Iranian men who crossed by small boat scouted a UK synagogue for a chlorine bomb
stories.summary: Two Iranian men who crossed the English Channel by small boat were ordered held until Oct. 23 after a prosecutor said they scouted Manchester’s Heaton Park synagogue and the Jewish Museum for a homemade chlorine bomb directed by a third person believed to be in Iran. Salam Ahmadyan, 36, and Rahman Salehi, 34, were charged with preparing terrorist acts. Salehi was granted asylum and Ahmadyan has a claim pending. The synagogue was the site of last year’s Yom Kippur knife attack that killed two congregants. Police said the case is separate from a suspected plot at the U.S.-run RAF Fairford base.

stories.headline: Hegseth says some U.S. troops could shift from Europe to the Western Hemisphere
stories.summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said Saturday that some U.S. troops could move from Europe to the Western Hemisphere as the administration expands its campaign against drug cartels in Central and South America. He tied the shift to President Trump’s capture of Nicolas Maduro and to new partnerships with Ecuador, Honduras, Guatemala, and Panama, and said the defense strategy calls for more burden-sharing by Europe.

stories.headline: France’s student riots called a cautionary tale for America’s open-border years
stories.summary: Fox News framed France’s student riots Saturday night as a warning for the United States, with “The Big Weekend Show” co-host Tomi Lahren calling the unrest a “cautionary tale” about open-border immigration. She said Europe treated diversity as a strength, that the Biden administration tried the same approach, and that the Trump administration is now undoing it.

stories.headline: Cornell’s president says the university ‘must do better’ on sexual-assault allegations
stories.summary: Cornell President Michael Kotlikoff said Saturday the university “must do better” after sexual-assault allegations involving seven former fraternity brothers. In a video to campus he called what happened to a student identified as Jane Doe in 2024 “deeply disturbing,” and said the case raises questions about party culture, alcohol and drugs, and the investigation that followed.

stories.headline: Cotton refuses Trump’s push for permanent daylight saving time
stories.summary: Sen. Tom Cotton answered President Trump’s demand that Arkansans pressure him on permanent daylight saving time, writing that he will not support the bill. Cotton said Congress has tried year-round daylight time before and repealed it after “absurdly late” winter sunrises, and that “Arkansans don’t want their kids going to school in the pitch dark.”

stories.headline: White House: DSA policies would cost about $355,000 per household over 10 years
stories.summary: A White House Council of Economic Advisers report, “The Real Cost of Socialism in America,” says seven Democratic Socialists of America policies that can be scored against the federal budget would cost more than $49 trillion over ten years, about $355,000 per household. The council warned of double-digit inflation that could reach 160 percent, higher mortgage rates, and job losses. President Trump posted Friday that the agenda would “completely destroy” the country and told supporters to vote Republican.

stories.headline: FBI’s Summer Heat 2.0 made nearly 9,000 arrests and located more than 1,400 children
stories.summary: The FBI said Operation Summer Heat 2.0 produced 8,927 arrests and the location of 1,410 children in violent-crimes-against-children cases between June 1 and Sept. 20. The bureau described it as the second year of a nationwide push that pairs federal agents with state, local, and tribal police.

stories.headline: Defending Education ranks red states highest on parental rights and DEI policy
stories.summary: A new Defending Education “RISE” ranking puts Tennessee, Alabama, Florida, North Carolina, and Iowa at the top on parental rights, DEI, gender policy, teacher rules, and foreign influence, and puts D.C., Illinois, Oregon, California, and Rhode Island at the bottom. Terry Stoops said states at the bottom have “sacrificed educational excellence at the altar of social justice,” and Paul Runko said parents need that information to choose schools.

stories.headline: A 12-year-old girl is killed in a Baltimore park shooting over a parking dispute
stories.summary: A 12-year-old girl was killed and three adults were wounded Saturday when two gunmen opened fire during an apparent parking dispute near Baltimore’s Leon Day Park while youth football was underway nearby. Commissioner Richard Worley called the shooters cowards and said the girl was likely there to watch the game. A 25-year-old woman and two men, 23 and 28, were hit. Their injuries were not life-threatening. Police were still looking for both gunmen.

stories.headline: Loudoun elementary teacher charged with assaulting a student
stories.summary: Loudoun County sheriff’s deputies charged Horizon Elementary teacher Valerie Bowen, 49, of Ashburn, with assault and battery after a school resource officer was told of an alleged Oct. 1 incident with a student. She was issued a summons, and the district said she is on leave while the sheriff’s office and the school system both review the case.

stories.headline: Route 66’s Bagdad Cafe is fighting to stay open as the Mother Road turns 100
stories.summary: The Bagdad Cafe in Newberry Springs, California, a Route 66 landmark made famous by the 1987 film of the same name, is fighting to stay open as the Mother Road turns 100. Longtime owner Andrea Pruett died in January, and the kitchen has been closed since the pandemic. The desert stop is still covered in flags, plates, and travelers’ notes, but its future is uncertain.

stories.headline: Voivod cancels its October U.S. tour over a family health emergency
stories.summary: Voivod canceled a 10-city October U.S. tour with BAT, which was set to open Oct. 8 in Youngstown, citing a family health emergency. The band said it cannot commit to new dates and that tickets will be refunded. The cancellation follows news that drummer Michel “Away” Langevin’s brother, Carol, was diagnosed with pancreatic cancer, while former singer Eric Forrest has been filling in on the road during his own cancer treatment.

stories.headline: Westport school board advances a $17.7 million capital plan, holds back Staples field work
stories.summary: Westport’s school board on Thursday unanimously advanced a $17.7 million capital plan that leaves out nearly $1 million of Staples High athletic-field work, including wireless access and a structure for concessions, restrooms, and team space, until a master-plan study finishes this fall. Superintendent Thomas Scarice said he does not want the district to “dig twice.” Plans for a girls’ team room and locker-room renovation at Staples were also pulled.
